cohort: Four women experiencing profuse hemorrhage from partially detached placentas following advanced extra-uterine pregnancies, one of whom is a 33-year-old primigravid woman.
finding: The Foley catheter tourniquet is a novel, simple, and effective surgical technique for controlling acute hemorrhage from partially detached placentas in extra-uterine pregnancies, leading to good surgical outcomes.
mod_finding: The primary case involved the delivery of an infant from an extra-uterine gestation sac via laparotomy for an abdominal pregnancy.
followup_time: The mother was discharged after 10 days and the baby after 21 days post-operation (with the tourniquet removed after 4 days).
